mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1.2M for the current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below the median baseline at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% for three consecutive months, combined with a deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.0% month-over-month, signals labor market and output weakness that reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% for three consecutive months AND INDPRO < 1.0% MoM for current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods (p > 0.10), or the mechanism fails during a period of strong earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals persistent supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% MoM for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of high commodity price shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% in response to a CPI inflation surge above 5% (CPIAUCSL) signals an emergency easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 5.0% in the same month
regime_hint: inflation shock followed by emergency easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the mechanism fails when the drop in rates is not accompanied by a clear inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 300,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and ultimately leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 300000 AND UNRATE < 3.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when wage growth accelerates sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% YoY, combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals pent-up household savings with weak aggregate demand, which suppresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5% YoY for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails when fiscal stimulus is introduced.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.0 million units for five consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.
